The optimal compression is upper bounded by the cost of a maximum traveling salesman tour in H, which in turn is upper bounded by the cost of a maximum cycle cover. The latter can be computed in polynomial time using matching, similar to the way we computed a minimum weight cycle cover. Since H has no self loops, each cycle has length at least 2. Remove the lightest edge from each cycle of the maximum cycle cover to obtain a set of disjoint paths. The sum of weights of edges on these paths is at least half the optimal compression. Overlap strings
according to the edges of these paths and concatenate the resulting strings. This gives a superstring achieving at least half the optimal compression.
